Antoninus Pius. Adopted by Hadrian around 138 CE, this Roman emperor presided over two decades of unprecedented peace and prosperity, with no major military conflicts or succession crises. He built the Antonine Wall in Scotland and strengthened provincial economies through trade routes and improved legal codes. Known for pious governance and public works, he consolidated the empire at its territorial apex, reaching the zenith of the Pax Romana before the empire's gradual decline.
